To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of L2 input in the form of L2 texts, and the use of L1 input in the form, of L1 texts, can facilitate L2 reading comprehension, but only when the L1 text provides a more accessible and comprehensible version of the L2 text; 2) the use of both L1 and L2 input in a text can facilitate L2 comprehension, when the L1 input provides a more accessible version of the L1 text,

(1) the most important factors for second language acquisition are the quality of the input and the amount of interaction; (2) learners are more successful when they are given a chance to interact with each other; and (3) teachers should use the language of instruction as a means for promoting interaction among students.
1. Second Language Learning and Teaching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of language learning in a naturalistic setting.
the nature of language learning and the implications of that learning for the design of instructional materials.
the nature of second language acquisition in a variety of contexts and with the development of pedagogically useful principles and techniques for teaching a second or foreign language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best method of teaching a second language is to teach the language in context and to use it for the purpose for language was designed: communication.
the principles of second language acquisition should be applied to language teaching practice in order to produce a more successful learning environment for the students.
the principles of second language acquisition can and should be used to guide second language teaching practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the most important factor in second language acquisition is the quality of the interaction between the learner and the teacher.
language learning occurs when learners have a reason to communicate.
language acquisition occurs when the learner is motivated to communicate and is given the opportunity to do so in a supportive, low-anxiety environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the principles of effective language instruction are not specific to a particular method or language but are applicable across languages and contexts.
the principles of second language acquisition are the same as those of first language acquisition.
the most important factor in second language learning is the quality of the classroom instruction, and the quality of the teacher, not the language program itself.
